evals.name: first-time-multi-thread-detection
evals.prompt: I've been working on the CLI auth refactor for a while and just got it tested end-to-end. While we're here, let me also start thinking about the marketing landing page redesign for next quarter. Where should the hero image go?
evals.expected_output: Agent should: (1) detect this is a multi-thread session (CLI work + marketing landing — orthogonal themes), (2) create DIRECTIONS.md if absent, with Pool 1 = CLI auth refactor (seeded from history) and Pool 2 = Marketing landing redesign, (3) flag the drift inline at the top of the reply ("Note: you're on Pool 1 (CLI auth). This prompt is pulling toward a new Pool 2 (Marketing landing). I'll add it as SEED — say 'pivot' to switch focus or 'park it' to come back later"), (4) answer the hero image question normally after the flag, (5) write the updated DIRECTIONS.md to disk.

evals.name: explicit-pool-view-query
evals.prompt: where am I in all this? what was I working on?
evals.expected_output: Agent should: (1) read existing DIRECTIONS.md from project root, (2) render the live pool view inline (preserve pool headers, theme descriptions, status flags, the 'leading edge' synthesis paragraph), (3) NOT append a new entry to DIRECTIONS.md (this is a view query, not a new direction), (4) NOT flag drift (no new direction opened), (5) end with a one-line orientation question like 'Want to refocus on Pool X, or stay on the current edge?'

evals.name: same-pool-subthread-no-drift
evals.prompt: Now let me also fix the JWT refresh edge case where the token is rotated mid-request. We're already in the auth refactor, this should slot in.
evals.expected_output: Agent should: (1) recognize this is a SUB-THREAD of the existing leading pool (auth refactor), NOT a new pool, (2) NOT flag drift (sub-threads of the leading pool don't drift), (3) add the JWT-refresh entry under Pool 1 with status LEADING, (4) answer the auth question normally without any drift-flag preamble, (5) update DIRECTIONS.md silently. Critical: the 'let me also' phrase is NOT a drift signal by itself — the orthogonality test matters more.
